lines.description: AN3 alloy-steel hex-head airframe bolt, cadmium plated, 10-32 thread, drilled shank, length not stated
lines.clarification_question: Line 1 asks for AN3 bolts, drilled, but gives no length. AN3 bolts come in 54 lengths in our catalog, each a different part number. Which dash number do you need? For example: (a) AN3-15, 1-21/32 in nominal, 1-1/4 in grip; (b) AN3-20, 2-1/32 in nominal, 1-5/8 in grip; (c) AN3-30, 3-1/32 in nominal, 2-5/8 in grip; or reply with the exact part number.
lines.notes: Family, diameter, thread, and drilling are known. The dash number decides the part number, so no match or price until the buyer answers.

standard.explanation: AN3 is the standard designation for the 3/16 in hex-head airframe bolt family.

form.explanation: AN3 is a hex-head airframe bolt family; the buyer also wrote bolts.

material.explanation: From the catalog: AN3 bolts are alloy steel. Not stated in the RFQ.

finish.explanation: From the catalog: cadmium plated. Not stated in the RFQ.

diameter.explanation: AN3 is the 3/16 in (0.1875 in) diameter family.

thread.explanation: AN3 family thread is 10-32, from the catalog.

drilling.explanation: A plain AN3 dash number is a drilled shank. The A suffix would mean undrilled.

quantity.explanation: Quantity and unit stated by the buyer. pcs means pieces, each.

assumptions: Drilled is read as drilled shank, the plain AN3 designation. The buyer did not say head or shank.
Material, finish, thread, and diameter come from the AN3 family in the catalog, not from the RFQ words.
rules_used: AN part number parser: family AN3 found, no dash number, so no part number.
Readiness rule: hardware needs a full part number or every field that determines one. Length is missing.

match.reason: 54 AN3 catalog items fit the stated fields. The dash number is needed to choose one.
